body:
Second read (read-only, not built) of head 8bae4e111d6c35d514d00b3e3266a22ad0502fc8.

**Verdict: no blocker found by reading.** The PR holds the stated law in all 20 shipped posts. I found three minor findings and two test gaps (below). None of them is a changed legal program, an unguarded post or a wrong position after a dropped arc.

## 1. Where the guard is, and the posts

One rule is in the prelude: `arcFateOf` / `arcFate` in `crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs`. `Script::load` appends it (`crates/post/src/post/js.rs` line 102). Each script calls it with its own word function.

| Post | Arc output | Guarded | By |
|---|---|---|---|
| carvera | yes | yes | `onCircular`, `arcFate(arcWord)` (`wo`, `fu`) |
| doosan-dnm | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` |
| fanuc | yes | yes | `onCircular` line 1060, after `compRefuse`, before `useRadiusArcs` |
| fanuc-lathe | yes (meridian G02/G03) | yes | `meridianArc`, `arcFateOf` on `xWord` / `zWord` |
| grbl | yes | yes | `onCircular` |
| grblhal | yes | yes | `onCircular` |
| haas | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` |
| heidenhain (DIN/ISO) | yes (G02/G03, `verticalArc` chords) | yes | `onCircular`, before `verticalArc` and the I/J block |
| heidenhain-klartext | yes (CC/C) | yes | `onCircular`, `local()` words |
| linuxcnc | yes | yes | `onCircular` |
| mach4 | yes | yes | `onCircular`, `arcFateOf` on the machine-frame values after `transformPt`, same `fu` |
| mazak | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` |
| sinker-iso | no (refuses each arc) | not needed | `onCircular` refusal, unchanged |
| sinumerik | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` |
| sodick-wire | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after `cutOk`, XY words only |
| tinyg | yes (G2/G3 halves, chords) | yes | `onCircular`, before the segment loop |
| tormach | yes | yes | `onCircular`, before `indexed()` and `useRadiusArcs` |
| tormach-lathe | yes (meridian) | yes | `meridianArc` |
| tormach-plasma | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after the compensation refusal |
| wire-iso | yes | yes | `onCircular`, after the taper refusal |

A search for every G2/G3 emission site in `assets/posts/*.cps` found no arc block outside these paths. The R-word paths (`emitArcWithRadius`, `buildSegs`) are after the guard. The Klartext CC/C blocks and the Heidenhain I/J block are after the guard. No post writes `CIP`, `CT` or a polar arc.

## 2. The comparison

- Each call uses the script's own word function: the same origin, unit and decimals as the written words (`wo` + `fu`, Klartext `local`, the lathe `xWord` diameter, mach4 `fu` on the transformed point).
- The plane frame is (X, Y) for G17, (Z, X) for G18 and (Y, Z) for G19, with the normal axis as the helix test.
- No post suppresses an unchanged X/Y/Z word (no `lastX` tracker; `xyz()` writes all axes). So the comparison of the two written words is the comparison with the control's position.
- Drift: a "none" arc has all written words equal at its start and its end. So the next record's start writes the same words that the control holds. A "linear" arc writes its own end. The invariant "the control holds the written words of the next record's start" is kept, and no error adds up over N dropped arcs. Each later real move goes to its own written end. Confirmed by reading.

## 3. The replacement

- A short helix becomes the script's own `onLinear` to the stream end. The XY words do not change, so a straight Z move is within one output step of the helix. The feed word is the record's own `FeedRate`.
- Each `onLinear` writes `G1`/`G01` explicitly, and each arc block writes `G2`/`G3` explicitly. So the modal group stays consistent after a suppressed arc.
- No empty `G1` line: "linear" comes only when Z or a rotary letter is present, and `xyz()` always writes the axes.
- Pending cutter compensation: `compRefuse` (fanuc, doosan, haas, mazak, sinumerik) and the mach4 / plasma refusals run before the guard. So a comp word never rides a sub-step "linear" move. The other posts refuse G41/G42 by name.

## 4. Full circles and arcs just above the step

- A full circle as two halves: each half has different written ends, and posts as before (pinned in table (b)).
- A circle under the output step: each half has sweep pi (not more), so it posts as no block. If float noise makes the sweep a little more than pi, it posts two full circles of sub-step size. The tool moves less than one step, so this is not unsafe.
- An arc with a written chord of one step: start and end differ, so it is not a full circle by the coincident rule. The I/J words come from the stream start, so the start/end radius mismatch at the control can be about one step. That is the same as on main. A radius-tolerance alarm is possible but not more frequent than before.

## 5. Goldens

No golden file changed (diff stat: no `tests/golden/`, no recorded stream). Programs with normal arcs are byte-identical: table (b) compares each post's full output with a reference stream that has only the normal arcs.

## 6. Tests

- `tiny.cnc` is recorded and matches the reporter's reproduction on #3442.
- Table (b) has all 20 posts. That is the same list as point 1. It runs mm and inch where `programUnits` offers inch, and R mode where the script has `useRadiusArcs`.
- The body says (a), (b) and (c) were red on main and are green on this head. I did not run them.
- The `radius_arcs.rs` and `tinyg_post.rs` changes each remove an assertion that pinned the fault. The `#[test]` count does not go down.

## Findings (none is a blocker)

1. **Minor. A missing centre is not refused when the written ends coincide.** `arc_guard.rs`, `arcFateOf`: when `c[u]` or `c[v]` is not a number, `round` is false and the result is "none" or "linear". Scenario: a full-turn record with equal stream ends and no I/J. Before, sodick-wire ("an arc states no centre"), heidenhain DIN ("arc without an XY centre") and tinyg refused it by name. Now it posts no block, with no diagnostic. Recommendation: return "arc" when the centre is not finite, so that each script's own refusal runs.
2. **Minor. The full-turn test uses exact equality.** `arcFateOf`: `full = s[u] === e[u] && s[v] === e[v]`. A one-record full turn whose stream end differs from its start by float noise gets its sweep from `atan2`. If the noise puts the end a little ahead of the start, the sweep is nearly 0. Then a full helical turn becomes a straight Z move. On a 10 nm stream lattice this is unlikely. `emitArcWithRadius` uses a 1e-5 mm band for the same test. Recommendation: use the same band.
3. **Minor, outside the stated law. A radial one-step chord.** If the written chord is radial to the written centre (the start within half a step of the centre's X or Y line, only the radial axis word changes), the written start and end have the same angle. A control that adds a full turn for an equal angle (the LinuxCNC and Fanuc arc rule) can cut a near-full spiral. By reading, this needs a radius under about 0.05 mm (mm) or 0.3 mm (inch) on the 10 nm stream lattice. It is rare and it is not made by this PR. Recommendation: a `P7` follow-up, or a written cross-product test (no positive turn sense on the written words means a short arc).

## Test gaps

- No test pins the "near-full turn with coincident written ends posts as one full circle" branch. The reporter asked for that case on #3442. Table (b) has full circles only as two halves.
- No test has a rotary letter on a short arc (the `rotary` branch of `arcFateOf`).

## Law

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new non-test Rust (`arc_guard.rs`, the `js.rs` hunk).
- The script text and comments are our own. The provenance line is in `arc_guard.rs`.
- `Changelog:` line: present. Decision file `docs/decisions/3442-coincident-arc-blocks.md`: present, with chosen, why and dropped. The body credits the reporter.
- Heavy lanes: the body says "not run yet". The PR must stay a draft until they ran on the final head.

## Not judged without a run

- The red-on-main and green-on-head results of the four new tests.
- The heavy lanes and the app suites that the body did not run.
- The stream frame against the written frame in 3+2 sections of the posts other than mach4. I assume that the stream is already in the local frame there.
- The behaviour of a real control on the one-step arcs of finding 3.

ready for a re-read: head 40e1baae7e0b6ebe6057aa20072f69fab3d9aa1a. The second-read findings 1 and 2 are fixed, and the two test gaps are closed (see the body, "Added after the second read"). The heavy lanes run next under the heavy-run lock.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head 40e1baae7e0b6ebe6057aa20072f69fab3d9aa1a.

**Verdict: one blocker, for the claim that the fix closes #3442 in the app.** The blocker was already present at 8bae4e111. I did not see it in my first read. The delta closes my two earlier findings, but it adds the opposite error below the band. No golden changed. Only `tinyg.cps` and `heidenhain.cps` changed among the posts.

## Blocker: the app's stream turns a sub-micrometre arc into a full turn

- `crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs` line 337 (`q`), lines 366-392 (`serialize`): the app writes each position and centre as whole micrometres. `crates/app/src/posting.rs` line 714, `posting_per_op.rs` line 230 and `posting_mounts.rs` line 339 post through `cnc::serialize`. `post/mod.rs` line 538 copies each arc without a chord test.
- #3463 states that `machining2d/fillet.rs` can emit a chord of about 0.09 um. The fit and biarc arcs have no chord floor, and they can have a large radius.
- Scenario: a fillet arc with a 0.09 um chord. `q()` rounds its start and its end to the same micrometre. The stream record now has its end equal to its start, with the centre off the start.
- `arc_guard.rs` line 61: `full` is true, so the result is "arc". Each post then writes `G03 X<start> Y<start> I.. J..`, which is a full circle. On a fit arc with a 50 mm radius, that is a 100 mm circle through the part.
- At the stream, this record cannot be told apart from a true full turn. The true sweep is known only before `q()`.
- Severity: blocker for `Fixes #3442`. The PR body says "The posts are safe after this PR" for #3463, and that statement is not correct.
- Recommendation: in `serialize` (or where `post/mod.rs` builds the `MoveRec`), write an arc whose rounded in-plane ends are equal, and whose true sweep is less than a full turn, as a `Feed` to its end (or as no record if nothing moves). Pin it with a `Toolpath` that has a 0.09 um fillet arc, posted through the app path.
- If this is moved to a separate issue, that issue is `P1`. The PR must then say `Refs #3442`, not `Fixes`.

## My earlier findings: closed

1. Centre missing. `arc_guard.rs` line 54 returns "arc" before the band. Trace: start = end = (1, 0) with no centre gives "arc", so the sodick-wire, heidenhain DIN and tinyg refusals run. The rule test pins it (`nocentre arc`, `nocentre-short arc`). The `.cnc` reader refuses an arc without centre words (`cnc.rs` line 819), so a rule-level pin is the right level. Closed.
2. Float noise on a full turn. Line 61 uses a 1e-5 mm band. Trace: a helical turn that ends 1e-6 mm off its start gives "arc", not "linear". This is pinned by `a_full_helical_turn_off_by_float_noise_stays_a_helix` over all mill posts and units. Closed.

## Finding (minor): the band does not use the arc's direction or centre

- The rule now has two parts:
  1. Ends within 1e-5 mm in the stream: a full turn, for any direction and sweep.
  2. Ends further apart, and coincident as written: the sweep from `atan2` with the direction and the centre. More than pi means a full turn. Otherwise the arc is short ("linear" or "none").
- So only above the band does the rule use the direction and the centre to separate a sweep near 0 degrees from a sweep near 360 degrees. Below the band, a TRUE short arc (sweep near 0, chord under 10 nm, centre off the start) becomes a full circle. That is the opposite error.
- The test delta shows it. The first witness arc changed from `Y 5432.03` to `Y 5432.02`. At the old values, the second arc (5432.03 to 5432.04 um) has a float chord of 9.9999999996e-6 mm, under the band, and it would now post a full circle.
- Reach: only a `.cnc` text with fractional micrometres. The reader accepts such text. The app stream is on a 1 um grid, where the blocker above applies.
- `tinyg.cps` line 667 and `heidenhain.cps` line 566 use the same end-point band.
  - On a 1 um grid, the tinyg change makes no difference: equal ends already gave a full sweep there.
  - The heidenhain `verticalArc` change does make a difference. Equal ends gave d = 0 before, which was one `G01` to the start: no motion. Now they give a full circle of chords. A true XZ/YZ full turn is now right. But a sub-micrometre XZ arc collapsed by `q()` now cuts a full circle, where before it did not move.
- Recommendation: use the band only with the sweep. An example: a full turn when the ends are within the band AND (the ends are equal, or the sweep from `atan2` is more than pi). The writer fix above removes the grid case.

## The new tests

- Near-full turn: a record 20 nm short of a full turn (`Y 5432.04` to `5432.02`). The 2e-5 mm gap is above the band, so the sweep path decides (about 2 pi, so "arc").
  - Fanuc and the other one-block dialects post one full-circle block, byte-identical to the exact full turn. Only that block has its written start equal to its written end.
  - tinyg posts two half blocks with different written ends.
  - Klartext refuses by name.
  - This is correct.
- Rotary: on fanuc with `tilthead.mch`, the arc with `A 1000` posts as a `G01` with `A1.` and no arc block. `onLinear` sets the modal state through `tilt()` / `heldAngles`, and no arc state is written. So no stale modal state remains. Only fanuc is tested. The other posts reach the same `onLinear` path, but no test runs it.
- The rule test pins direction cases (`short-cw-is-near-full arc`, `xz-short-cw arc`). Good.

## Other checks

- No golden and no app file changed in the delta. The 17 other guarded posts did not change.
- The decision file is updated for the band and the centreless case.
- The heavy lanes are still not stated as run on this head. The PR must stay a draft.

## Not judged without a run

- The 8 `coincident_arcs` results and the post-crate binaries that the author reports.
- Whether a present generator emits a sub-micrometre arc in a real program. #3463 lists the sites by reading only.

ready for a re-read: head 532d0fa92e34305c545cdddb6b27ff1e0638051d. The blocker is fixed in the stream writer (crates/post/src/post/cnc_arc_lattice.rs, called by cnc::serialize). The 1e-5 mm band is dropped. New tests: short_arc_lattice (app, red on the old writer), cnc_arc_lattice (post), and the rule cases. No golden changed. The heavy lanes run next under the lock.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head 532d0fa92e34305c545cdddb6b27ff1e0638051d.

**Verdict: no blocker found by reading.** The blocker of my last read is closed for every app posting path. The band is gone, and the opposite error with it. I found three minor findings (below). No golden changed. Among the posts, only `heidenhain.cps` changed (`verticalArc`), and `tinyg.cps` is back to its first-head text.

## 1. The writer covers each app path

- `cnc::serialize` (`crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs` line 371) calls `cnc_arc_lattice::short_arc_on_lattice`. It is the only writer of `.cnc` arc records in `crates/*/src`. A search for `"Arc {` and `Arc CCW` / `Arc CW` found no other writer.
- These paths use it:
  - The whole job: `posting.rs` line 691.
  - Per operation: `posting_per_op.rs` line 230.
  - Per mount: `posting_mounts.rs` line 339.
  - The preview: `preview.rs` line 109.
  - The section mode: `section_mode.rs` line 131.
- `commands/post.rs` line 51 posts an empty stream (a script check only).
- The app test `short_arc_lattice.rs` pins the three posting paths in mm and inch with a 0.09 um fillet on R50.
- The simulator reads the `Toolpath`, not the stream, so it shows the true arc.

## 2. The writer rule

- The rule uses the true geometry before rounding. `pos` is the true end of the last move (line 372). The sweep comes from the true start, end, centre and direction.
- True sweep between pi and 2 pi with ends that round to one micrometre: the arc record is kept with equal ends, and the reader takes it as a full turn. This is correct. The true path is a full turn short by less than 1 um on each axis. That gap is below the 1 um stream step, and below or at the step of each post (mm 0.001, inch 0.0001 in). Klartext writes 0.1 um, but the stream has already lost the gap there.
- Sweep of exactly pi: `<=` gives a `Feed`. Rounded ends can be equal only when the diameter is under about 1.4 um. Then the tool is less than 1 um off the path. It is safe either way.
- A short helix: the `Feed` carries the rounded Z (pinned: `Feed X 0 Y 0 Z -1000`).
- With no known start (the first record, or after `Touch` / `Retreat` / `Guard`, lines 468-477), the arc is written as before.
- The generators write a full turn as halves (`entry.rs` line 96, `trochoid_bore.rs`, `thread_ride.rs`). `push_arc` writes exactly equal ends as a line (`cl/path.rs`). So by reading, no generator gives a one-record full turn.

## 3. The zero-length Feed

- Each post writes `G1`/`G01` (Klartext: `L`) with all axis words, because `xyz()` always writes them. The program gets a legal zero-length line, not an empty line and not a bare `G1 F`.
- The F word is the arc's own feed, so the modal feed for the next move is the same as with the arc.
- `sinker-iso` refused each arc. A collapsed sub-micrometre arc in a sinker job now reaches its straight-move path. That is acceptable.

## 4. The reader and the format

- An arc record with equal ends in the stream is a full turn. The decision file now states that this is the meaning of the format (`full_circle_raw`). Our own writer no longer uses that form for a short arc.
- A hand-written `.cnc` file with a short arc and equal micrometre ends is read as a full circle. That is now the documented meaning of the format.
- The reporter's `tiny.cnc` (ends 1 um apart) reaches the post guard and posts no arc block. Pinned by (a).

## 5. No band

- `arc_guard.rs` line 64: a full turn is either exactly equal ends, or a sweep of more than pi from the direction and the centre.
- A helical turn whose end is 1e-6 mm BEHIND its start: the sweep is nearly 2 pi, so the result is a full turn ("arc"). Pinned by `noise-behind arc` and by the mill test with `Y 5431.999`.
- A record whose end is 1e-6 mm AHEAD: the result is "linear". By its own geometry it is a short helix. See finding 1.
- The witness is back to `5432.03` to `5432.04` um, a 10 nm chord. Its ends are not exactly equal, the sweep is about 1e-9 rad, and the result is "none". The opposite error is closed.

## 6. Heidenhain and tinyg

- `heidenhain.cps` line 566: only exactly equal ends make `d` a full turn. The writer no longer gives equal ends for a short arc, so a collapsed sub-micrometre XZ/YZ arc from the app becomes a straight move. A stated full turn is now a full circle of chords. Before #3442 it was one zero-length `G01`, so this change is correct.
- `tinyg.cps`: back to the first-head text. Equal ends give a sweep of 0 plus a full turn, which agrees with the format.

## 7. Scope

No golden file changed in this delta. The other 18 posts did not change.

## Findings (none is a blocker)

1. **Minor. A one-record full turn with float noise AHEAD of its start becomes a straight move.** `cnc_arc_lattice.rs` lines 51-60 and `arc_guard.rs` line 64. Scenario: a generator writes one full helical turn whose true end is 1e-12 mm ahead of its start. The writer finds a sweep of nearly 0 and writes a `Feed`, which is a straight Z plunge where the program needs a helix. By reading, no present generator does this (see point 2). Recommendation: record in the decision that a full turn must be written as two halves, or that a one-record turn needs exactly equal ends. A `debug_assert` or a test on `push_arc` can hold that law.
2. **Minor. The CL text writer has no lattice rule.** `crates/cl/src/cl/text.rs` line 105 (`to_text`) writes arcs in micrometres without `short_arc_on_lattice`. `camcraft-post` accepts a `.cl` dump as input (`crates/post/src/bin/post.rs` line 23). So a `.cl` dump of a sub-micrometre arc, posted with the CLI, is still read as a full turn. Today only tests and `camcraft-motion` (facing, no arcs) write `.cl`. Recommendation: a `P7` follow-up, or the same rule in `to_text`.
3. **Minor, still open from my first read. A radial one-step chord.** A short arc near a quadrant point can round so that only the radial axis changes by 1 um, while the centre's cross axis rounds to zero. The written start and end then have the same angle. A control that adds a full turn for an equal angle can cut a spiral. This is rare, and this PR does not cause it. Recommendation: a `P7` follow-up.

## Not judged without a run

- The new tests (`short_arc_lattice` 2, `cnc_arc_lattice` 2, `coincident_arcs` 8) and the claim that `short_arc_lattice` was red without the writer.
- The heavy lanes. The body must state that they ran on this head before the PR leaves draft.

Heavy lanes on the final head 532d0fa92e34305c545cdddb6b27ff1e0638051d: **green**.

- Command: `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6 cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main`, on the head itself, with `origin/main` at ef1572114.
- Summary line: `wall 55.8 min, 207 step(s), 0 failed`.
- Lanes that ran: one release build and the `app heavy` targets (206 steps: `lib`, `bins`, `doc` and the integration targets, with `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `posting` and the post tests of each dialect). The plan reached no kernel lane and no motion lane.
- Known-fail probes, red as expected: `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` (#1950, `tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`) and `fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (#2849, `tests/shoulder_adaptive.rs`).
- No golden file changed in the run (`git status --short -- crates/app/tests/golden` is empty).

Not covered by this run: the head does not contain the current `main` (51 commits behind). The quick gate and the example catalog suites on the trial merge with the current `main` come next. The PR is flagged ready after that run is green.
